..body

KEY POINTS 
* Pier A Pump Station No. W-028 (PS28) is one of the largest storm water pump stations within the Port of Long Beach (Port). It is critical that facilities such as this one are maintained in good operating condition to ensure areas they serve do not flood and Port operations can continue uninterrupted during storm events.
* PS28 is near the end of its service life, and significant rehabilitation of the facility is required.  The Pier A Pump Station No. W-028 Rehabilitation project (Project) will upgrade the facility ensuring it has sufficient pumping capacity for storm events and is outfitted with current monitoring and controls technology.
* The Engineering Design Division solicited for professional engineering services for the design of the Project and selected Cannon Corporation (Cannon) for the work.  
* The proposed design contract is for a not-to-exceed amount of $3,731,400 and a term extending to July 31, 2029.
* Cannon is a Small Business Enterprise. Cannon's commitment plan represents 100% Small Business Enterprise (SBE)/Very Small Business Enterprise (VSBE) of which 5.04% is allocated to VSBE, thus exceeding the combined 30% SBE/5% VSBE goal for this contract.
* If approved, construction of the Project is anticipated to be completed in 2028.

DISCUSSION

Background

The Port owns and/or maintains approximately 34.5 miles of storm drain within the Harbor District. The Port complex has 33 pump stations within its boundaries. PS28 is owned and operated by the Port, and is one of the largest pump stations within the Port complex. It is critical that facilities such as this one are maintained in good operating condition to ensure areas they serve do not flood and Port operations can continue uninterrupted during storm events.  

A thorough inspection of PS28 was performed in December 2020, and it was determined that significant rehabilitation of the facility is required.  The Project will upgrade the facility ensuring it has sufficient pumping capacity for storm events and is outfitted with current monitoring and controls technology.  

Current Issues 

A professional engineering consulting firm is needed to develop a design for the Project.

Selection Process 
A Request for Proposals (RFP) to provide professional engineering design services for the Project was posted on PlanetBids. A total of 1,966 firms were notified directly of the solicitation. Staff performed additional outreach to notify vendors of this solicitation at various professional industry organization meetings. In addition, the RFP was posted on the Port's LinkedIn page and X (formerly Twitter) feed to ensure maximum outreach to a diverse audience of potential interested parties. During the solicitation period, 70 firms downloaded the documents. Two proposals were received before the proposal deadline. Both firms were interviewed. Based upon scoring and selection criteria, Cannon was recommended as the most qualified firm to provide professional engineering design services for the Project. Staff negotiated with Cannon for a fee and labor rates that are considered fair and reasonable. Attachment A provides additional details on the selection process.

Approve a Baseline Project Budget in the amount of $47,455,000 and Authorize Spending in the amount of $6,905,000 to complete the design, bid and award phases for the Shoemaker Bridge Ramps Demolition project. (Program Management - M. Lebrun)
..body

KEY POINTS  
* The Pier B On-Dock Rail Support Facility Program (Pier B ODRSF Program) will improve the Port of Long Beach's (Port) on-dock rail network, enabling a mode shift from truck to train supporting the goal of moving 35% of all Port cargo by on-dock rail, and reducing the carbon footprint of the supply chain.
* The Shoemaker Bridge Ramps Demolition project (Project) will demolish and remove the 9th and 10th Street ramps west of the Los Angeles River.  
* The Project will clear the way for future utility relocations and rail expansion work.  
* The proposed Baseline Project Budget is $47,455,000 and, if approved, the Project is expected to be substantially completed in early 2027.
* The Project includes grant funding from the California State Transportation Agency (CALSTA).

DISCUSSION

Background
The Pier B ODRSF Program is a key component of the Port's 10-Year Capital Plan, the centerpiece of all planned rail infrastructure representing our commitment to operational excellence. The Program will reconfigure and expand the existing Pier B Rail Yard, to support the increased use of on-dock rail at the Port, reducing the carbon footprint of the supply chain.  

2024 is an exciting year for the Pier B ODRSF Program. The first project, the Pier B rail Yard East Expansion, has been advertised for bids, and construction is scheduled to begin later this year.  The second project, the Pier B Rail Yard Locomotive Facility project, is scheduled to be advertised for bids in May of this year.  Furthermore, five additional projects are advancing through various stages of design.  One of the Pier B ODRSF projects currently in the design phase is the Shoemaker Bridge Ramps Demolition Project.  The Project will demolish and remove the two existing ramps west of the Los Angeles River and clear the way for future utility relocations and rail expansion work.  

The Project includes the following elements:

* Modifications to traffic striping and signage and installation of traffic control systems.
* Demolition and removal of the existing eastbound ramp, including approach, abutments, superstructure, and columns from 9th Street and Caspian Ave to the existing southbound Shoemaker Bridge connection in the existing freeway median. 
* Demolition and removal of the existing westbound ramp, including approach, abutments, superstructure, and columns from 10th Street & Caspian Ave, across the 710 freeway nearly to the LA River where the ramp diverges from the northbound Shoemaker Bridge lanes.
* Excavation and grading of approach ramp fill areas.

Current Issues 
The project has achieved the 50% design milestone and in accordance with the Port's Program/Project Budget Approval and Accounting Policy, staff has prepared a proposed Baseline Budget.  With approval by the Board of Harbor Commissioners (Board), staff will advance the design of the project to completion, and at that point, return to the Board to request consideration of approval to advertise the Project for construction bids.

This Project requires close coordination and permits from the Los Angeles County Flood Control District, US Army Corps of Engineers, and Caltrans.  Additionally, the project is adjacent to the Shoemaker Bridge Replacement Project, led by Long Beach Public Works Department.  Both the Port and Public Works are closely coordinating to facilitate the timely and efficient completion of both projects.

Not Applicable

Contract Compliance and SBE Information
Not Applicable

CEQA Determination  
The requested action has been reviewed by the Director of Environmental Planning and determined to be a subsequent approval within the scope of the Environmental Impact Report for the Pier B On-Dock Rail Support Facility Project certified by the Board of Harbor Commissioners pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act and issued Harbor Development Permit 07-021 on January 22, 2018, under resolution HD-2906.

FINANCIAL IMPACT 
Spending authorization in the amount of $6,905,000 is being requested to complete design, bid and award of the Project. If approved, the total Board authorized spending will be $9,455,000.  Approval of a Baseline Project Budget of $47,455,000 is also requested. Funding for this Project is included in the Fiscal Year 2024 Capital Program Budget. The Project includes grant funding in the amount of $14,105,576 from the California State Transportation Agency (CALSTA) for Port and Freight Infrastructure Programs.

The requested spending authorization can be accommodated in the Current Program Budget of $1.567 billion. Staff continues to monitor the local and national construction cost trends.  We are also collaborating with agency partners on strategies to help mitigate pass-through inflation risk from contractors.

Staff will conduct a holistic analysis of the Current Program Budget in 2024 utilizing the results of the monitoring of local and national construction cost trends, actual costs incurred for property acquisitions, and actual bids received for oil field relocation work and the first Pier B ODRSF construction contract.  Staff forecast reporting the results of this analysis and with any recommendations to the Board in the fourth calendar quarter of 2024.

KEY POINTS
* The Pier B On-Dock Rail Support Facility Program (Pier B ODRSF Program) will improve the Port of Long Beach's (Port) on-dock rail network, enabling a mode shift from truck to train supporting the goal of moving 35% of all Port cargo by on-dock rail, and reducing the carbon footprint of the supply chain.
* Bid documents for the second Pier B ODRSF Program project, the Pier B Locomotive Facility (Project), are being finalized for advertisement for construction bids in 2024, and certain items specified are required to match other products currently in use at the Port.
* Sole source for Tracsis (formerly known as RailComm) Railroad Signal Control System is required to match other products in use at the Port for maintenance and operation of the entire rail network within the Port area and the Alameda Corridor.
* Sole source for Calsense Irrigation Controller is required to match other products in use at the Port and to ensure compatibility with the other irrigation controllers throughout the Port's network.  

DISCUSSION

Background
The Pier B ODRSF Program is a key component of the Port's 10-Year Capital Plan representing our commitment to operational excellence. It will reconfigure and expand the existing Pier B Rail Yard, to support the increased use of on-dock rail at the Port, reducing the carbon footprint of the supply chain.

Considerable progress has been made on the Pier B ODRSF Program thus far, with six projects currently advancing through the design phase and one in the bid and award phase. 
The next project, the Pier B Rail Yard Locomotive Facility Project will be advertised for bids shortly.  The Project will construct new tracks specifically for the servicing of up to 30-locomotives. Project improvements include:

* Demolition of fencing and paving, and clearing and grubbing the site.
* Construction of a locomotive facility with six storage tracks and associated turnouts.
* Special track-work, including turnouts and crossovers, railroad signals, and realigning and resurfacing the existing mainline track.
* Construction of communication and power duct banks, high mast light poles, and control panels.
* Rail signal system modifications at Control Points Gaspur & Perry.
* Construction of utilities and associated appurtenances.
* Landscaping and street frontage improvements along East I Street.
* Storm water quality, treatment, and diversion systems.

Current Issues 
In recent years, the Port of Los Angeles and the Port of Long Beach began installing RailComm switches that can be radio controlled by locomotive crews and a proprietary railyard operations management system in the rail network shared by both ports.  Sole sourcing the subject switch control work will ensure it is compatible with the existing switch control and dispatch system, and is necessary for maintenance and operations of the rail system.  RailComm has since been acquired by, and rebranded as, Tracsis.

Similarly, sole sourcing the Calsense Irrigation Controller is required for compatibility with the other irrigation controllers throughout the Port's network. 

The City Attorney's Office has reviewed the proposed request for sole source procurement and has determined it complies with the provisions of California Public Contract Code Section 3400, which allows for sole sourcing to match existing products in use on a public works project.  

Staff recommends the following items be sole sourced under Specification HD-S3136 for the Pier B Rail Yard Locomotive Facility project:

* Railroad Signal Control System by Tracsis (formerly RailComm, Inc.) 
* Irrigation Controller by Calsense

CEQA Determination  
The requested action has been reviewed by the Director of Environmental Planning and determined to be a subsequent approval within the scope of the Environmental Impact Report for the Pier B On-Dock Rail Support Facility Project certified by the Board of Harbor Commissioners pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act and issued Harbor Development Permit 07-021 on January 22, 2018, under resolution HD-2906.

FINANCIAL IMPACT 
It is estimated that these items will cost approximately $168,000, budgeted within the Project.  Funding for the Project is included in the approved Fiscal Year 2024 and proposed Fiscal Year 2025 Capital Program Budgets.  The Project includes grant funding from the US Maritime Administration's (MARAD) 2021 Port Infrastructure Development Program (PIDP) and the California Transportation Commission's (CTC) 2022 Trade Corridor Enhancement Program (TCEP).  MARAD has approved the sole source proposal for the subject two items for the PIDP grant.  CTC does not require an approval process for the TCEP grant.

KEY POINTS 
* The proposed Sewer Lift Station 101 project (SLS 101 Project) would provide a backup generator which would allow the lift station to operate during power outages.
* SLS 101 is the largest sewer lift station within the Port of Long Beach (Port), serving Piers F, G, H, and J. 
* The backup generator would be integrated into the Port's existing Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system to facilitate effective monitoring and operation of SLS 101.
* The preliminary Project design has been completed and a proposed Baseline Budget, in the amount of $3,345,000, developed for the Project.  If approved, the Project is expected to be substantially completed in early 2026.

DISCUSSION

Background
The Port owns and maintains 38 sewer lift stations.  Preventative maintenance and prompt repairs are crucial for uninterrupted operations. Inoperable sewer pumps can cause raw sewage backup and overflow, posing health risks.

SLS 101 is located along Harbor Scenic Drive, between Ocean Blvd. and the Queensway Bridge.  It collects sewer flows from Piers F, G, H, and J tributary areas and discharges to a Pico Avenue sewer main running north to the Los Angeles County Sanitation District sewer system for processing and treatment at their wastewater treatment facility. This is the largest sewer lift station in the Harbor District.  A backup generator is needed so that SLS 101 remains operational during a power outage.

The preliminary design for the proposed Project has been completed and in accordance with the Port's Program/Project Budget Approval & Accounting Policy, staff has prepared a proposed Baseline Project Budget. ..body


KEY POINTS 
* All Port of Long Beach (Port) waterfront facilities and terminals are inherently co-located where the ocean meets the endpoints of storm drainage infrastructure, where the management of stormwater is at its peak demand and is a requirement for the operation of these facilities and terminals.
* Pumping equipment required to accomplish this task within the Port is both unique and very large.
* The Maintenance Division is responsible for maintaining all sewer and storm drain pumping equipment within the Port. At present, the Port's Maintenance Facility lacks a pump shop suitable for performing repairs, oftentimes, necessitating outsourcing repairs which is both costly and time consuming. 
* The proposed Maintenance Building C Pump Shop Conversion project (Project) will reconfigure space in an existing building at the Maintenance Facility, enabling Division staff to maintain and repair pumping equipment in-house, saving cost and time, and helping ensure this critical component of our infrastructure is on-line and serving its purpose, keeping our waterfront facilities and terminals free from flooding. This pump shop will also facilitate regular inspections, diagnostics, and preventive repairs, thereby minimizing the risk of unexpected failures.
* The Project includes installing workbenches and equipment for pump inspections and repairs, a crane for moving large and heavy pump components, and the associated utilities, appurtenances and staff facilities.
* The Engineer's Opinion of Probable Construction Cost is $1,220,000, and if approved the Project is expected to be substantially completed by mid-2026.




DISCUSSION

Background
The Port's storm drain and sewer infrastructure includes 60 pump stations (38 sewer, 22 stormwater) maintained by the Maintenance Division. Preventative maintenance and prompt repairs are crucial for uninterrupted operations. Inoperable sewer pumps can cause raw sewage backup and overflow, posing health risks. Failing stormwater pumps can lead to property damage and disruption of Port operations.

The existing Port Maintenance Facility lacks a pump shop, leading to reliance on outside vendors for maintenance and repairs. This reliance creates vulnerability, as vendor backlogs can result in lengthy pump repair turnaround. Converting an existing maintenance space into a fully functional pump repair facility will enable in-house repairs, reducing downtime and operational disruptions. 

The Project includes the following elements:
* A bridge crane, enabling the safe and efficient lifting and movement of large and heavy pump components for disassembly, repair, and reassembly.
* Work benches strategically positioned throughout the shop, including a designated electrical test bench for comprehensive diagnostics and repairs.
* A supervisor's office and restroom.
* Fire suppression system.
* Storage racks for pumps, pump components, tools, and other necessary supplies.
* Utility systems (i.e., water, plumbing, power, communications).  

Current Issues 
The contract documents for the proposed Project will be ready to advertise for bids by November 2024. If approved, the Project is expected to be substantially completed by mid-2026.

Selection Process 
Advertising the contract specification to solicit bids to construct the Project is the first step in the selection process for the proposed contract.  Upon receipt and review of the bids received, staff will request the Board of Harbor Commissioners (Board) consider conditional award of a construction contract for the Project to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder.

Contract Compliance and SBE Information
A combined Small Business Enterprise (SBE) /Very Small Business Enterprise (VBSE) goal of 27% of which 5% is allocated to VSBEs has been established for this contract.

CEQA Determination  
The requested action has been reviewed by the Director of Environmental Planning and determined to be categorically exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) under State CEQA Guidelines Section 15301 (Class 1 Existing Facilities) and Section 15303 (Class 3 New Construction or Conversion of Small Structures).

FINANCIAL IMPACT 
The Engineer's Estimate of Probable Construction Cost is $1,220,000. Once bids are received, staff will return to the Board requesting approval to execute a construction contract and spending authorization to complete the Project.  The Baseline Project Budget is $3,615,000.

Funding for the Project is included in the Fiscal Years 2024 and 2025 Capital Program Budgets.

(Program Management - M. Lebrun)
..body

KEY POINTS 
* The Middle Harbor Terminal Redevelopment Program (Program) has modernized two aging shipping terminals into a state-of-the-art container terminal.  
* The third phase of the program was completed in June 2021, enabling the terminal to operate at its full 3.3 million TEU per year throughput capacity.  
* The Pier E North Gate Expansion project (Project) will add two inbound truck lanes with truck scales, expand the existing Optical Character Recognition (OCR) building, and add additional area for truck troubleshooting all of which adds approximately three acres to the terminal, expanding the final terminal acreage to approximately 303 acres, completing all aspects of the buildout of this terminal.  
* The Engineer's Opinion of Probable Construction Cost is $14,050,000, and the Project is expected to be substantially completed in the first quarter of calendar year 2026. 

DISCUSSION

Background
The Program consisted of combining Piers D, E, and F to form a modern contiguous approximate 303-acre terminal.  Construction of the terminal included new gates, buildings, wharf structures, rail mounted gantry cranes, container and intermodal rail yards, landfill, paving and striping, and utility infrastructure.  Phase 1, the northern half of the terminal, comprised 150 acres and was completed and turned over to the tenant, Long Beach Container Terminal (LBCT), for operations in April 2016. Phase 2 added an additional 41 acres in October 2017.  Phase 3 completed construction in June 2021, increasing the total acreage to 300 acres.  The North Gate Expansion project expands the final terminal acreage to approximately 303 acres.

Although the terminal is fully operational, the expansion of the terminal's North Gate, stipulated in the Preferential Assignment Agreement with LBCT, LLC (HD-7918), could not be constructed until after the Gerald Desmond Bridge was demolished and removed.  The remaining scope covered in the Project includes adding two inbound truck lanes with truck scales, expanding the existing OCR building, and adding a truck parking and troubleshooting area in the terminal's North Gate.

Current Issues 
Contract documents for construction of the Project are ready to be advertised for bids subject to approval as to form by the City Attorney. If approved, construction is expected to start in the first quarter of calendar year 2025, with completion expected in the first quarter of 2026.

Terminal infrastructure was designed to be interconnected and a system was installed to allow LBCT to control and monitor equipment including fire alarms and electrical equipment for terminal buildings and infrastructure. Staff recommends specifying products for this project that match those competitively bid and installed in previously constructed Middle Harbor projects. 

The provisions of California Public Contract Code Section 3400, allow for sole sourcing to match existing products in use on a public works project. The products listed below were competitively bid and installed under the previously constructed Middle Harbor projects. Sole sourcing these products will ensure compatibility with the existing equipment and more efficiency in operations and maintenance of the equipment. The City Attorney's Office has reviewed the proposed request for the sole source procurement and has determined it complies with the California Public Contract Code Section 3400 that allows for sole sourcing to match existing products already in use on the existing public works projects. Staff recommends the following equipment be sole sourced:

1. Fire alarm system by Notifier
* The existing alarm system was manufactured by Notifier. The fire alarm system uses proprietary signaling and communication protocols to maintain system integrity and cannot be mixed between manufacturers. Therefore, the new alarm system must match existing for the existing controls to function properly.
* Maintenance of the alarm system is simplified by using the same alarm system.

2. Truck scales by Fairbanks
* The existing truck scales were manufactured by Fairbanks. The new truck scales must match existing to align with scale pit footprint and maintain consistency with controls. Having the same truck scales ensures all dimensions match and proper tie-in with the existing truck scales.
* Maintenance of the new truck scales is simplified by using the same scales. 

3. Electrical equipment Panel boards by Square D:
* The existing terminal medium voltage switchgear and related electrical equipment including electrical panel boards are manufactured by Square D. The new electrical equipment panel boards must match existing to properly communicate with the existing system. 
* Maintaining consistency in equipment and parts across the terminal simplifies maintenance, troubleshooting, and spare parts management.

4. High mast light poles luminaire by Holophane
* The existing high mast light poles (HMLPs) luminaire is manufactured by Holophane. Maintaining uniformity in the lighting fixtures across the terminal avoids reduction in existing system functionality, provides uniform light output and color temperature across the terminal, and streamlines maintenance procedures, repairs, and replacements. 

Selection Process 
Advertising the contract specification to solicit bids to construct the Project is the first step in the selection process for the proposed contract.  Upon receipt and review of the bids received, staff will request the Board of Harbor Commissioners (Board) consider conditional award of a construction contract for the Project to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder.

Contract Compliance and SBE Information
A combined Small Business Enterprise (SBE)/ Very Small Business Enterprise (VSBE) goal of 27%, of which 5% is allocated to VSBEs has been established for this contract.

CEQA Determination  
The requested action has been reviewed by the Director of Environmental Planning and determined to be a subsequent approval within the scope of the Environmental Impact Statement/Environmental Impact Report for the Port of Long Beach Middle Harbor Redevelopment Project certified by the Board of Harbor Commissioners on April 13, 2009 under Resolution HD-2498 pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA).

FINANCIAL IMPACT 
The Engineer's Estimate of Probable Construction Cost is $14,050,000. Once bids are received, staff will return to the Board requesting approval to execute a construction contract and spending authorization to complete the Project.  The Baseline Project Budget is $14,800,000 and the Current Program Budget is $1.493B.

Funding for the Project is included in the Fiscal Years 2024 and 2025 Capital Program Budgets.

KEY POINTS 
* The Port of Long Beach (Port) has 123 Ford trucks, vans and SUVs, which at times require Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) parts and service for both regular and emergency repairs to maintain proper operating condition, maintain warranties, and to extend their useful lives. 
* The Maintenance Division's Fleet Section services the Port's fleet and requires Ford OEM parts and in some cases service by Ford repair technicians with specialized certification, training, and diagnostic equipment that cannot be provided in the Port's garage.  
* The Long Beach City Council (City) approved Specification No. ITB 23-313 for a contract for the purchase of Ford OEM parts and service from South Bay Ford, Inc. (South Bay Ford). 
* The City requires enterprise Departments to execute their own contracts for the parts and service they need.
* The Maintenance Division is recommending the Port "piggyback" on the City's procurement and execute a Port-specific contract (City Pass-Through Agreement) in the amount of $500,000. The contract will expire January 27, 2026, and have options for three additional one-year extensions, matching provisions for the contract being executed by the City. 
* Section 1802 of the Long Beach City Charter allows the Port to purchase goods and services procured by another government entity (in this case, the City of Long Beach), called "piggybacking". This saves considerable time and funding in the contract procurement process.






DISCUSSION

Background
The Maintenance Division's Fleet Section is responsible for maintaining in proper operating condition the Port's fleet which includes but is not limited to 123 Ford trucks, vans and SUVs. Access to Ford OEM parts and Ford repair technicians, with specialized certification, training and diagnostic equipment, allows timely repair of complex and specially outfitted equipment that cannot be repaired in the Port's garage. 

On December 5, 2023, the Long Beach City Council approved ITB FM 23-313 authorizing the City Manager to award a contract to South Bay Ford for the purchase of Ford OEM parts and service. 

Current Issues 
Due to the similarities in the City and Port fleets, the City's contract with South Bay Ford offers an ideal service and value, which the Maintenance Division would like to utilize. The City now requires enterprise Departments to execute their own specific contracts for the parts and service they require.

Selection Process 
Section 1802 of the Long Beach City Charter allows the Port to purchase goods and services procured by another government entity (in this case, the City of Long Beach), called "piggybacking". This saves considerable time and funding in the contract procurement process. 

The Maintenance Division recommends the Port "piggyback" on the City's procurement and execute a Port-specific contract (City Pass-Through Agreement) to purchase Ford OEM parts and service.   This contract will expire January 27, 2026, and have the option for three additional one-year extensions, matching provisions for the contract being executed by the City.

Contract Compliance and SBE Information
There are no small business enterprise goals associated with this procurement.

The Port's Central Procurement Services Division facilitated the procurement process.  


FINANCIAL IMPACT 
The Maintenance Division budgets for automotive parts and repair services on an annual basis. The proposed $500,000 contract capacity is estimated to be sufficient to support planned and unanticipated repair of the Port's Ford trucks, vans, and SUVs.  This contract is a time-and-materials type contract for which the Port will only pay for actual parts and services authorized and rendered.

KEY POINTS 
* The Port of Long Beach (Port) provides diesel and unleaded fuel for vehicles and equipment not yet transitioned to zero-emission equivalents. Port fueling locations require continuous maintenance and support services to comply with regulations and to ensure that equipment is available for both routine and emergency response. 
* The Board of Harbor Commissioners (Board) approved a contract with Western Pump in the amount of $400,000 on January 24, 2022 for these services.  
* The First Amendment is proposed for to extend the term of the contract one-year until a new contract is established. 
* The value of the contract will remain unchanged. A new rate sheet is included for the proposed extended term.  This rate sheet has been reviewed by Maintenance staff and deemed appropriate based on comparison to relative market rates.   

DISCUSSION

Background
The Maintenance Division provides vehicle and emergency generator fueling at multiple locations throughout the Port complex including the Maintenance Yard, Joint Command and Control Center (JCCC), and five storm water pump stations. These facilities may include fuel islands, dispensers, storage tanks and related control and monitoring systems, which require regular maintenance and support. Specialized and systems-certified vendor support is required to comply with regulations and meet operational expectations for uninterrupted fueling service. 

Current Issues 
If approved, the proposed First Amendment to this contract will extend the term one-year to March 16, 2026 while a new contract for these services is procured.  The amendment also includes a new rate sheet for the extended term, updated insurance, and specific prevailing wage requirements.

Selection Process

KEY POINTS 
* All Port of Long Beach (Port) waterfront facilities and terminals are inherently co-located where the ocean meets the endpoints of storm drainage infrastructure, where the management of stormwater is at its peak demand and is a requirement for the operation of these facilities and terminals.
* Pumping equipment required to accomplish this task within the Port is both unique and very large.
* The Maintenance Division is responsible for maintaining all sewer and storm drain pumping equipment within the Port. At present, the Port's Maintenance Facility lacks a
pump shop suitable for performing repairs, oftentimes, necessitating outsourcing
repairs which is both costly and time consuming.
* The proposed Maintenance Building C Pump Shop Conversion project (Project) will reconfigure space in an existing building at the Maintenance Facility, enabling Division staff to maintain and repair pumping equipment in-house, saving cost and time, and helping ensure this critical component of our infrastructure is on-line and serving its purpose, keeping our waterfront facilities and terminals free from flooding. This pump shop will also facilitate regular inspections, diagnostics, and preventive repairs, thereby minimizing the risk of unexpected failures. 
* Contract documents were advertised for bids on January 30, 2025 and three bids were received on March 25, 2025.
* US Builders and Consultants, Inc. made a clerical error on the bid submitted, and requested to withdraw the bid. The request US Builders and Consultants, Inc. made to withdraw its bid has been reviewed and approved by the City Attorney's Office.
* After consulting with the City Attorney's Office, staff recommends the bid submitted by Newman Midland Corporation be declared non-responsive for failure to meet the Port's Performance History requirement of having a Worker's Compensation Experience Modification Factor (Ex-Mod) less than 1.25. 
* Staff recommends that the Board of Harbor Commissioners (Board) award a construction contract to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder, Milender White Construction Co. (Milender White), in the amount of $2,535,175.02.
* Milender White submitted a Small Business Enterprise (SBE)/Very Small Business Enterprise (VSBE) commitment totaling 8.01% of which 8.01% was allocated to SBE, which did not meet the combined SBE/VSBE goal. However, Milender White submitted a Good Faith Effort (GFE), which was evaluated by Port staff and received a passing score. 
* If approved, it is estimated that construction will be substantially complete by the fourth quarter of fiscal year (FY) 2026.

DISCUSSION

Background
The Port's storm drain and sewer infrastructure includes 60 pump stations (38 sewer, 22 stormwater) maintained by the Maintenance Division. Preventative maintenance and prompt repairs are crucial for uninterrupted operations. Inoperable sewer pumps can cause raw sewage backup and overflow, posing health risks. Failing stormwater pumps can lead to property damage and disruption of Port operations.

The existing Port Maintenance Facility lacks a pump shop, leading to reliance on outside vendors for maintenance and repairs. This reliance creates vulnerability, as vendor backlogs can result in lengthy pump repair turnaround. Converting an existing maintenance space into a fully functional pump repair facility will enable in-house repairs, reducing downtime and operational disruptions. 

The Project includes the following elements:

* A bridge crane, enabling the safe and efficient lifting and movement of large and heavy pump components for disassembly, repair, and reassembly.
* Work benches strategically positioned throughout the shop, including a designated electrical test bench for comprehensive diagnostics and repairs.
* A supervisor's office and restroom.
* Fire suppression system.
* Storage racks for pumps, pump components, tools, and other necessary supplies.
* Utility systems (i.e., water, plumbing, power, communications).  

Current Issues 
Staff concluded an evaluation of construction bids received for the Project and recommends approval of the conditional award of a construction contract to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder, a Current Budget, and spending authorization to complete the Project.

Selection Process 
The Project was advertised for bids on January 30, 2025 through postings on PlanetBids, various local newspapers (including the Long Beach Press-Telegram, Our Weekly Newspaper, and Random Lengths News), and the Port's social media channels, including LinkedIn and X (formerly known as Twitter), to maximize outreach to a diverse audience of potential interested parties. KEY POINTS 
* On July 6, 2023, the California State Transportation Agency (CalSTA) awarded the Port of Long Beach (the Port) $383.35 million in Senate Bill 198 Port and Freight Infrastructure Program (PFIP) grant funding for the System-Wide Investment in Freight Transport (SWIFT) project which included $158,402,000 in construction funding for the Port's Pier B On-Dock Rail Support (Pier B ODRSF) Program.
* The grant award will fund three project components within the Pier B ODRSF Program: LA 04 Pump Station, assigned $60,990,000; Shoemaker Bridge Ramps Demolition, assigned $42,025,000; and Rail West Expansion, assigned $55,387,000.
* The PFIP program requires execution of a Master Agreement between the California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) and the local agency receiving grant funds. Master Agreement No. 75SR0019CTC between Caltrans and the City of Long Beach is effective as of April 28, 2022. There is no requirement for a Baseline Agreement with Caltrans under the PFIP grant program.
* The Program Supplement Agreement (PSA) No. 00000A798 is an agreement between the Port and Caltrans (the grant administering agency) that sets the terms and conditions for project delivery by the Port and reimbursement by the grantor agency.
* The PSA allows the Port to submit reimbursement requests to Caltrans for work on the LA-04 Pump Station project component.

DISCUSSION

Background
In July 2023, the Port of Long Beach was awarded $383.35 million in California Port and Freight Infrastructure Program (PFIP) grant funding from the California State Transportation Agency for the Port's SWIFT project. This award includes $224.95 million for Port tenant electrification projects and $158.40 million for the Pier B ODRSF Program (the largest state grant awarded to the Pier B ODRSF Program). The PFIP grant funding is assigned to the following Pier B ODRSF project components:
* LA 04 Pump Station - $60,990,000 
* Shoemaker Bridge Ramps Demolition - $42,025,000 
* Rail West Expansion - $55,387,000
Typically for state grant funding, a Baseline Agreement defines the project's benefits, scope, schedule, and budget, and is followed by a Program Supplemental Agreement (PSA) which authorizes the Port to begin drawing down grant funds. Under the PFIP program, a Baseline Agreement between the Port and Caltrans is not required - only relevant PSAs would be needed. Each PSA corresponds to a discrete project component with its own construction contract. Because PFIP omits the Baseline Agreement requirement, the PSA will serve as the primary project-specific agreement between the Port and Caltrans, authorizing the reimbursement of PFIP funds for construction activities. 
On August 26, 2025, the Board of Harbor Commissioners approved Resolution No. HD-24-3217, authorizing the Port's Chief Executive Officer to execute Project Supplemental Agreements (PSAs) without Board action. DISCUSSION

Background
The Pier B On-Dock Rail Support Facility Program (Pier B ODRSF Program) is a key component of the Port's 10-Year Capital Plan representing our commitment to operational excellence. The Program will construct an expanded on-dock rail facility, re-align Pier B Street and Pico Avenue, establish new utility corridors, provide surge capacity for the railroads and terminals by expansion of storage tracks, all while reducing the carbon footprint of the supply chain. 

In support of the larger program, the LA-04 Pump Station Relocation Project (Project) will construct a new storm water pump station and decommission the existing Los Angeles County Flood Control District (LACFCD) storm water pump station, making way for subsequent expansion of the Pier B On-Dock Rail Support Facility. Current Issues 
Due to the size of the Port's Capital Program, the Port utilizes a combination of in-house resources and consultant services to deliver the current and forecasted peaks in workload. In-house resources are assigned first to projects strategically, based on expertise, availability, as well as to further develop in-house expertise for key types of work. The Port then solicits consultant services to deliver the projects that comprise the remaining peak workload. After a thorough review of the Capital Program and in-house assignments, it was determined that consultant services are needed to supplement in-house resources to deliver this significant
Program.

If approved, Mott MacDonald will provide CM services for the Project including: participating in preconstruction and partnering meetings; construction administration; conducting weekly construction progress meetings; maintaining project records; administrative and document control; coordination of review of submittals, coordination of requests for information; performing schedule reviews, estimating, claims evaluation support, and utility coordination; coordination of construction activities with the contractor, Port staff, tenants, utility owners, adjacent construction contractors, and other stakeholders; preparing weekly reports, change orders and Board Memoranda; review and processing of progress payment requests; evaluation of work and developing recommended courses of action.

The proposed contract term is for three years. Mott MacDonald is committed to 22 percent SBE/VSBE participation.  This exceeds the Port's goals for this solicitation of 20 percent SBE/VSBE.

Selection Process 
In May 2025, a Request for Proposals (RFP) for Construction Management Services for the LA-04 Pump Station Relocation project was published on the Port's e-procurement vendor portal. A total of 3,871 vendors were notified in PlanetBids of the bid opportunity; 115 prospective bidders downloaded the RFP documents and 24 vendors attended the pre-proposal meeting. The solicitation closed in June 2025 and nine (9) proposals were received. After an independent and thorough evaluation of proposals received and interviews conducted, it was determined that Mott MacDonald Inc., a new vendor to the Port, was the top ranked vendor and was selected for contract award. 

The Central Procurement Services Division facilitated the solicitation and execution of this contract on behalf of the Construction Management Division.

* The backup generator will be integrated into the Port's existing Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system to facilitate effective monitoring and operation.
* The contract documents were advertised for bids on August 28, 2025, and four bids were received on October 14, 2025.

Background
The Port owns and maintains 38 sewer lift stations.  Preventative maintenance and prompt repairs are performed to provide uninterrupted operations. KEY POINTS 
* The Harbor Scenic Drive Roadway and Infrastructure Improvements project (Project) provides for replacing the existing pavement and implementing measures to enhance safe, reliable access and efficient operations for Port of Long Beach (Port) tenants and the public while reducing long-term maintenance costs. 
* The proposed Project will improve traffic flows for a critical component of the Port's roadway network at the terminus of the I-710 Freeway. 
* Staff recommends sole sourcing the irrigation equipment and video cameras to match existing products currently in use throughout the Port.
* The Project includes state grant funding in the amount of $26.9 million from the California Trade Corridor Enhancement Program (TCEP) and federal aid highway funding in the amount of $21.4 million from the Congestion Mitigation and Air Quality Improvement (CMAQ) Program.
* The Engineer's Opinion of Probable Construction Cost is $71.8 million, and the Project is expected to be substantially completed in the second quarter of calendar year 2028.
 

DISCUSSION

Background
Harbor Scenic Drive is an arterial connector to I-710 and a critical and heavily utilized transportation corridor within the Harbor District, serving Piers F, G, and J marine terminal areas as well as the Queen Mary, Carnival Cruise terminal, and future amphitheater areas on Pier H.  Harbor Scenic Drive will also be an important corridor for public access to many LA28 Olympic events. Harbor Scenic Drive frequently experiences congestion due to heavy truck traffic moving to and from the container terminals, which has contributed to deterioration of the pavement section. Staff has conducted a condition assessment of the Harbor Scenic Drive pavement in accordance with Port's Pavement Management System and determined the pavement is at the end of its useful life. The minimum acceptable target Pavement Condition Index (PCI) rating adopted for the Harbor District roadways is 65. Several areas of Harbor Scenic Drive have PCI ratings that fall well below 65 and requires replacement.

The Project includes pavement reconstruction between Ocean Boulevard and Harbor Plaza, along with other improvements that will enhance traffic flow and reduce congestion.  Improvements include the installation of changeable message signs, dedicated turn lanes, and intelligent transportation system components (sensors and cameras) for dynamic lane management. The roadway geometry will also be brought up to current Port and Caltrans design standards to improve safety.  In addition, the Project will upgrade signage, street lights, various utilities, and landscaping within the Project footprint.

Current Issues 
Contract documents for construction of the Project are ready to be advertised for bids, subject to approval as to form by the City Attorney. If approved, construction is expected to start in the first quarter of calendar year 2027, with completion expected in the second quarter of 2028.

The provisions of California Public Contract Code Section 3400 allow for sole sourcing to match existing products in use on a public works project. The irrigation and video surveillance equipment installed by this Project are required to match the Port's Maintenance Division and Security Division systems that are currently in use.  Sole sourcing these products is required for compatibility in operations and maintenance of existing equipment. The City Attorney's Office has reviewed the proposed request for the sole source procurement and has determined it complies with the California Public Contract Code Section 3400 that allows for sole sourcing to match existing products already in use on existing public works projects. Staff recommends the following equipment be sole sourced:

1. Irrigation Equipment:
* Calsense Controllers
* Calsense Flow Sensors
* Rain Bird Spray Heads
* Hunter Bubblers

2. Security Camera Equipment:
* Axis Cameras
* Hanwha Cameras
* Bosch Cameras
* Cisco Network Switches

Selection Process 
Advertising the contract specification to solicit bids to construct the Project is the first step in the selection process for the proposed contract. Upon receipt and review of the bids received, staff will request the Board of Harbor Commissioners (Board) consider conditional award of a construction contract for the Project to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder.

SBE Information
The combined Small Business Enterprise (SBE)/Very Small Business Enterprise (VSBE) participation goal proposed for this contract is 27% with 0% of that allocated to VSBEs. 

CEQA Determination  
The requested action has been reviewed by the Director of Environmental Planning. Construction activity associated with the Harbor Scenic Drive Roadway and Infrastructure Improvements Project will be performed under Harbor Development Permit HDP 24-066(1) issued on April 24, 2025, and was previously determined to be categorically exempt from CEQA pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines Section 15301 (Class 1. Existing Facilities), and Section 15303 (New Construction or Conversion of Small Structures).


FINANCIAL IMPACT 
The Engineer's Estimate of Probable Construction Cost is $71,813,712. Once bids are received, staff will return to the Board requesting approval to execute a construction contract and spending authorization to complete the Project. The Baseline Project Budget is $100,950,000.

The Project includes state grant funding in the amount of $26.9 million from Senate Bill 1 Trade Corridor Enhancement Program (TCEP) and federal aid highway funding in the amount of $21.4 million from the Surface Transportation Block Grant, Congestion Mitigation and Air Quality (CMAQ) Improvement Program for construction of the Project.

* The Port of Long Beach relies on its Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system, a network of integrated software and field sensors, to monitor stormwater and sewer pump stations. This capability is critical to preventing flooding, minimizing system failures, and avoiding sewage spills. 
* SCADA enables real-time system visibility, status updates and automated alerts for the Maintenance Division, supporting rapid response and operational continuity.
* SCADA monitoring is currently deployed at 5 of the Port's 55 pump stations, with planned expansion to an additional 10 stations, advancing broader systems visibility and resilience across the Port infrastructure.
* Effective support of SCADA and pump control systems requires specialized technical expertise that is not currently maintained within the Information Management Division, necessitating external support to ensure system reliability and performance.
* This contract provides ongoing critical services to sustain and enhance SCADA operations, including:
o Ongoing software support, maintenance, and upgrades for the SCADA computing environment
o Field support and troubleshooting for control system components at SCADA-enabled pump stations
o Technical consulting services to ensure third-party system design and integration align with Port standards
o Engineering Design and construction support for capital projects involving pump control systems.
* Tetra Tech will support several upcoming capital and utility programs that depend on SCADA and pump control systems, including the North Yard Utilities project, the Pier B Street Widening project, and the rebuild of Pump Stations 28 and 30.

Background
The Port's SCADA system enables staff to remotely monitor and manage pump station operations, including pump activity, water levels, electrical performance, gas detection, and backup generator status. The system provides real-time visibility and issues automated email alerts to the Maintenance Division team when abnormalities occur. 

Since its initial deployment in 2012, SCADA-enabled stormwater and sewer pump stations have required ongoing support for sensors, controllers, communication systems, and software to enable reliable and continuous operation.

Current Issues 
Maintaining reliable performance across existing and future SCADA-enabled pump stations requires specialized technical expertise in pump controls, industrial automation, and SCADA system management. 

Following a competitive Request for Proposals (RFP) process, Tetra Tech was selected as the qualified provider to deliver the necessary ongoing technical support, consulting services, and system enhancements necessary to sustain and expand operations.

In December 2025, an RFP for Implementation and Maintenance of Pump Station Control Systems and SCADA software was issued through the Port's e-procurement vendor portal. The RFP was also promoted via the Port's social media channels. In addition to broad notification through the Port's procurement portal (1,879 vendors), targeted outreach was conducted to 20 local and small business organizations and 9 technical firms.

 A total of 44 prospective bidders downloaded the RFP documents and 11 vendors attended the pre-proposal meeting. The solicitation closed in January 2026 and eight proposals were received. 

Following a comprehensive and independent evaluation process, including reviews and vendor interviews, Tetra Tech, Inc., an existing vendor, was identified as the highest-ranked proposer and was selected for contract award. The Central Procurement Services Division facilitated the solicitation and execution of this contract on behalf of the Information Management Division.

* The North Yard Utilities and Pier B Widening project (Project) will prepare for the future construction of the new railyard by relocating conflicting public utilities, developing underground infrastructure, modifying Pier B Street south of the new railyard, and constructing a new perimeter road north of the railyard.

DISCUSSION

Background
The Pier B ODRSF Program is a key component of the Port's 10-Year Capital Program, the centerpiece of all planned rail infrastructure, representing the Port's commitment to operational excellence. The Pier B ODRSF Program will reconfigure and expand the existing Pier B Rail Yard to support the increased use of on-dock rail at the Port, while reducing the carbon footprint of the supply chain. The Pier B ODRSF Program continues to progress in 2026; four projects are now in construction, three - including this one - will advertise for bids this summer, and the final three are progressing through the design phase.

The Project will build the roadway and public utility backbone for the Pier B ODRSF Program on a 77-acre project area extending from Pier B Street to 12th Street and from the Long Beach-Los Angeles city boundary to the 710 Freeway. The completion of this Project will clear the way for the Pier B ODRSF Program's rail expansion to 48-tracks. The Project includes the following elements:

* The relocation of certain public utilities, including street lighting, communications, sanitary sewer, storm drain, and water lines.
* Removal of abandoned and idle third-party utilities. 
* Construction of a new sanitary sewer lift station near 9th St and Anaheim St.
* Widening of Pier B Street from Edison Ave to Pico Ave from two to four lanes.
* Construction of a new perimeter road.
* Reconfiguration of Harbor Ave. and 11th St intersection.
* Reconfiguration of existing West 9th Street from Fashion Ave. to existing Caltrans and California Resources Corporation (CRC) access easement.
* Construction of a new retaining wall on the North side of Pier B Street.

Staff reviewed and evaluated the qualifications of all the applicants based on objective evaluation criteria and determined eight applicants met the minimum qualifications required for this Project. Based on the results of the evaluation, the following entities were deemed prequalified and eligible to submit bids on this project, listed in alphabetical order:

Background

Pump Station 28 was completed in 1997, and is now nearing the end of its useful life. The Project scope includes replacing all eight pumps, replacing the pump control system, replacing the backup generator, pipeline modifications, and structural repairs and modifications to improve future pump station operations and maintenance.
